experiments.guard: WIRING: clicking a Cost-window segment must actually select that window. tests/settings_cost.test.mjs calls window.chela.setCostWindow('7d') DIRECTLY and never touches the onclick attribute renderSettings() emits onto each .cost-window-btn — the same handler-vs-binding hop the round-3 verdict caught on the tab rail (closed there by _invokeOnclick) and that the orchestrator's round-4 comment named explicitly ('Do not satisfy it by calling selectSettingsTab() directly — that proves the handler, not the binding'). After this mutation the 7d button is a live, highlighted, no-op that re-fetches Live forever, and the attribute text still parses, still names a real window, and still reaches a real function.

the Cost tab's window switcher shows WHICH window is being displayed — _applyWindowButtons() is the only thing that moves .active / aria-pressed off the template's hardcoded Live default. settings_cost.test.mjs asserts the fetch URL and the re-rendered table after setCostWindow('7d') but never reads the segment's own state, so after this mutation no segment is ever marked selected (and aria-pressed stays 'true' on Live forever, which is what a screen reader announces) while the table below it silently shows 7d data.

notes: Round 4 (PR #358): both experiments above verified by hand — each mutation applied to the working tree turns tests/settings_cost.test.mjs red (test 4 'the Cost tab renders a project-grouped table...' and/or test 5 'clicking a rendered Cost-window segment...'), then reverted with a clean `git diff` before committing.
